messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the egress firewall shaper rolled at 03:10 UTC we saw GPU pool scaling stalls in AP-SOUTHEAST-1 canary.
maria: Symptoms: node provisioning took ~45s longer, ~12% of attach attempts timed out and retried. Affected dedicated pools only (reserved nodes).
ops-bot: alert: autoscaler.attach.fail count=18 region=ap-southeast-1 reason=KMS_DECRYPT_TIMEOUT timestamp=2026-03-19T03:23:11Z
maria: I checked control-plane logs; KMS decrypts to unwrap node bootstrap secrets spiked and failed behind NAT. Looks correlated with the egress shaping rule that tightened non-NAT HTTP egress.
raj: Do we have the exact rule that landed? I can revert if needed.
maria: Rule snippet rolled by infra-deploy at 03:10UTC:
```
allow egress to 10.0.0.0/8 via privatelink
deny egress 0.0.0.0/0 except nat-gw
throttle 10mbps per instance for port 443
```
maria: The throttle step appears to have reduced parallel KMS handshakes below what the keystore client expects during warmup.
sam: Are KMS calls going over the NAT or privatelink? If NAT, scaling NAT GW or switching keystore traffic to privatelink would help.
maria: Keystore is supposed to use privatelink but our fallback for a subset of bootstrap requests hits the NAT when interface-level failover occurs. Those concurrent retries + throttling = timeouts.
kelly: Quick mitigation: add explicit allow for the keystore privatelink endpoint CIDRs and remove the per-instance 10mbps throttle for control-plane subnets.
raj: Agree. Also we should temporarily increase NAT concurrency (or add an extra NAT GW) so logs/audit forwarding doesn't starve the decrypt calls.
alejandra: On the audit side: enabling KMS audit export to central S3 increased outbound connections during node churn. That pushed conntrack table high on our NAT instances.
sam: Ops plan suggestion:
  1) Add allowlist for keystore privatelink CIDRs (ap-southeast-1) — immediate (5m).
  2) Revert per-instance egress throttle for control-plane subnets — immediate (5m).
  3) Scale NAT GW capacity in the AZs for 30m — immediate.
  4) Canary in eu-west-1 for 2h, then ap-southeast-1 full rollout if stable.
maria: +1. I'll open a PR for the rule change and tag infra-deploy. I'll also push a temporary firewall exception and notify oncall.
raj: I'll prep the NAT scale command and a rollback playbook. Example to add route table entry for privatelink: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --destination-cidr-block 10.10.0.0/16 --network-interface-id eni-privatelink
```
maria: Monitoring to watch: autoscaler.attach.latency, keystore.decrypt.error_rate, nat.conntrack_used, node-attach-retries. If numbers drop back to baseline within 15 mins we can mark mitigated.
kelly: Also file a post-change note for the firewall team so future shapers consider bootstrap/control-plane bypass.
alejandra: I'll check audit export batching to reduce peak egress. Could buffer to reduce conntrack spikes.
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll post updates here after the canary. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-status: firewall-exception PR opened by maria (#4821) link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/4821 :eyes:
maria: update 03:28UTC: applied allowlist + reverted throttle in control-plane subnets. Early signs — attach latency is back to normal in the canary.
raj: I'll keep NAT scaled for 1h and then drop if stable. :white_check_mark:
maria: closing loop once canary passes. If anything else pops up ping me.
